abstract: Traditional coral taxonomy is increasingly challenged by recent advances in molecular evidence. Quantitative methods previously used to identify morphological descriptors have not been successful at detecting significant differences at the macroscale. It is of great interest to optimise methods for effectively delimiting species within the complex genus \textit{Acropora} to ensure sustainable, long-term management of these vital ecosystems. Topological Data Analysis (TDA) is designed to study the shape of data and can detect features that familiar methods overlook. This novel approach makes TDA and persistent homology a logical choice for studying coral morphology in a taxonomic context. The results show that valid topological information can be extracted from in-situ coral images and that there is great potential in further refining this method. This study is a first exploration into the potential of persistent homology in supporting the delimitation of the reef-building scleractinian corals \textit{Acropora}.

title: From Shape to Species: The Use of Persistent Homology in Restructuring the Taxonomy of \textit{Acropora} corals
